properties.name: The optimize skill's step 3 says "find the cause by measuring, never by guessing" and hands off to nothing — a session ran four ad-hoc hypotheses under it before Anthony pointed at /root-cause
properties.statement:
ANTHONY'S CORRECTION, 2026-09-12, mid-investigation: "Should be able to do /root-cause on any of these investigations." What he had watched: under /optimize, investigating why loop_status cost 12 s, the agent formed and tested four causes in a row (debug binary, shared transport, store compaction, the instrument) without opening the root-cause skill — the exact pattern that skill's own text records its author falling into "one hour after writing it". Every hypothesis WAS measured and falsified, so the work was not wrong; it was unstructured, and step ② (search the design for a precedent) was skipped — a prior finding that "the store is not why" (fact:the-orientation-reads-cost-ten-seconds-and-the-store-is-not-why) surfaced only later, from propagate_change.

THE SEAM: record_finding's description DEMANDS the root-cause skill before a cause is written, and that demand is what eventually caught the session. optimize's step 3 — "Write the hypothesis down, then design the cheapest experiment that could falsify it" — is root-cause's steps ③-⑤ restated, with no hand-off to the skill that holds them. So the moment the trigger fires ("that's odd", "it must be X") is inside a skill that describes the discipline without invoking it. The fix shape is the one 438 built for tools: the hand-off belongs IN the step, not in a catalogue (req:a-discipline-is-delivered-at-the-tool-not-in-a-catalogue).

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the same seam exists in other skills that contain an investigative step (check-health's "what is wrong here", impact-check's "what rotted"). Only optimize was measured, once.
